A consignment of edible oil with the vehicle in which it was carried was seized by the first respondent, suspecting non-compliance of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
Shunson C.J vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 June, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190914900/
2 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short).

sentences.text: The consignment and the vehicle are presently retained in the premises of Peramangalam Police Station.
The case of the petitioner is that the first respondent, the Food Safety Officer has no authority to seize and retain the vehicle.
According to the learned counsel, in a case of this nature, the Food Safety Officer can seize only the consignment of the article of food.

He, therefore, seeks the following reliefs:
"Call for the records and A) direct the first respondent to release KL-09-AD 7313 LMV Goods Carriage Bharath Benz Vehicles from the custody of the third respondent and hand over the possession of the vehicles to the petitioner with immediate effect.
B) to declare that the first respondent has no authority to seize or possess vehicles as per Food Safety and Standards Act, 2016 and rules and regulations thereof.
C) to grant the petitioner such other incidental reliefs including the costs of these proceedings."

2. Section 38(1) of the Act dealing with the powers of the Food Safety Officer reads thus:
"Powers of Food Safety Officer.- (1) The Food Safety Officer may- (a) take a sample- (i) of any food, or any substance, which appears to him to be intended for sale, or to have been sold for human consumption; or (ii) of any article of food or substance which is found by him on or in any such premises;
which he has reason to believe that it may be required as evidence in proceedings under any of the provisions of this Act or of the regulations or orders made thereunder; or (b) seize any article of food which appears to the Food Safety Officer to be in contravention of this Act or the regulations made thereunder; and (c) keep it in the safe custody of the food business operator such article of food after taking a sample;
and in both cases send the same for analysis to a Food Analyst for the local area within which such sample has been taken:
Provided that where the Food Safety officer keeps such article in the safe custody of the food business operator, he may require the food business operator to execute a bond for a sum of money equal to the value of such article with one or more sureties as the Food Safety Officer deems fit and the food business operator shall execute the bond accordingly.
Shunson C.J vs The Food Safety Officer on 1 June, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190914900/
3 x x x x x x x x"
A perusal of the said provisions indicates that the Food Safety Officer is not empowered to seize the vehicle in which the food articles were carried.
3.

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid facts, I deem it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition in the following manner:
(i) The articles of food seized from the possession of the petitioner shall be removed forthwith to a place under the control of the first respondent and the vehicle in which the seized food articles were carried shall be released to the petitioner.

(ii) If the first respondent is not able to find a place for keeping the seized food articles, the same can be kept in a place in the possession of the petitioner under the lock and key of the first respondent, until the standard of the food articles is ascertained.
(iii) If the seized food articles are found to be conforming to the standards prescribed under the Act, the same shall be returned to the petitioner.
Otherwise, the petitioner shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
